title: YouTube Videos as a Source of Misinformation on Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
screen_reason: Content analysis of the first 200 YouTube results for 'idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis' (102 eligible patient-directed videos), each evaluated by two respirologists against ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT clinical practice guidelines. The paper reports the share of videos presenting therapies NOT recommended in guidelines as valid and potentially beneficial treatments (17/102 = 17%), which the authors themselves call 'misleading and potentially harmful misinformation'. That is a CONTENT prevalence estimate against an external ground truth with a stated denominator. HONCode/DISCERN results are recorded as a QUALITY row, excluded from prevalence.

estimates.country: Videos hosted in North America 58 (57%: United States 45/44%, Canada 13/13%), Europe 31 (30%: Germany 17, UK 9, Switzerland 3, Scotland 1, Austria 1), Other 13 (India 2, Australia 1, Singapore 1, Thailand 1, Unknown 8); search performed on the U.S. version of YouTube from a U.S. IP address
estimates.measure_type: % of patient-directed IPF YouTube videos that described therapies not recommended in clinical practice guidelines as valid/beneficial treatments
estimates.denominator: 102 patient-directed YouTube videos on IPF meeting eligibility criteria, drawn from the first 200 search results (173 unique videos) for 'idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis'
estimates.definition: Video suggested at least one therapy not recommended in the ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT IPF clinical practice guidelines as a valid, non-experimental chronic management option (cannabis oil 2, corticosteroids 5, CPAP 1, enzymes 4, gluten-free diet 1, immunosuppressants 1, interferon 1, niacin 1, N-acetylcysteine 6, selenium 1, serrapeptase 1, stem cells 2, whey protein 1)
estimates.misinfo_def: No formal definition; the authors describe videos claiming their products provide a 'cure' for IPF as 'misleading and potentially harmful misinformation for patients and their caregivers', and the operational criterion is non-concordance with the 2011 diagnostic and 2015 treatment IPF guidelines
estimates.source_quote: Therapies that are not recommended in clinical practice guidelines were suggested in 17% of videos, including corticosteroids as a chronic treatment in 5% of videos
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two authors independently evaluated every video: GCG, a respirology fellow with an interest in interstitial lung disease, and SAG, a fully certified respirologist with ILD subspecialty training. Content scored against 30 predefined IPF features from the 2011 and 2015 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT clinical practice guidelines. Interobserver agreement for content: median 96% (92%-99%), kappa 0.85 (0.81-0.96), 'very good agreement'.
estimates.moderator_quote: The phrase "idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis" was searched for on the United States (U.S.) version of YouTube (youtube.com) on May 4, 2017, after removal of the web browsers' history and cookies. Country-specific results were standardized using a U.S. Internet Protocol (IP) address ... The first 200 identified videos (10 pages of results) were assessed for eligibility.
estimates.notes: Denominator is every eligible video in the topical search sample (items that exist) -> CONTENT. denom_selection=curated because the frame is the first 200 ranked search results. breadth=misleading: the numerator is guideline-discordant treatment recommendations (some outright false 'cure' claims, some merely unsupported), not verified falsehoods. country_norm=Multi-country because Table 1 enumerates the host countries of the 102 videos, even though the search itself was US-localised.  QUOTE NOTE: the v2 text extraction interleaves the article's columns, so no longer contiguous span of the published sentence is recoverable; source_quote is the exact contiguous span carrying the value, and the full published sentence is: "Therapies that are not recommended in clinical practice guidelines were suggested in 17% of videos, including corticosteroids as a chronic treatment in 5% of videos and N-acetylcysteine in 6%." (Results, p. 10); Table 4 row: "Any non-indicated therapy Overall (n=102) 17 (17%)".

estimates.country: Videos hosted in North America 57%, Europe 30%, Other 13%; search from a U.S. IP address
estimates.measure_type: % of patient-directed IPF YouTube videos with a HIGH HONCode quality/reliability score (6-8 of 8 principles)
estimates.definition: Video satisfied 6-8 of the 8 adapted Health on the Net Foundation Code of Conduct principles (sourcing, referencing, funding disclosure, advertising separation, etc.)
estimates.misinfo_def: n/a - HONCode measures reliability/credibility of presentation, not truth or falsity
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two authors scored each of the 8 HONCode principles 1/0; interobserver agreement median 95% (91%-97%), kappa 0.77 (0.69-0.93).
estimates.moderator_quote: Adherence to HONCode principles was evaluated for each video by two authors, with a score of 1 for adherence and 0 for non-adherence for each of the 8 principles.
estimates.notes: QUALITY by the INSTRUCTIONS' rule (HONCode/DISCERN-type instruments judge reliability and presentation, not veracity: a wholly true video with no references scores low). Recorded for completeness and to be EXCLUDED from prevalence. The DISCERN results and the median content score are not given rows because they are reported only as medians of a scale, not as shares.  QUOTE NOTE: the v2 text extraction interleaves the article's columns, so no longer contiguous span of the published sentence is recoverable; source_quote is the exact contiguous span carrying the value, and the full published sentence is: the quote is the full Table 3 HONCode row (overall, then by source category); the Discussion states "Only 7% of IPF-related videos had a high HONCode score, in contrast to a previous study reporting high HONCode scores in 69% of patient-directed videos on COPD."

missed_or_uncertain: (1) GEOGRAPHIC SUBGROUPS, for an adjudicator who wants them: 'Non-indicated therapies were recommended in 24% of videos produced in North America, as compared with 3% of videos produced in Europe and 15% of videos produced in other continents.' These are continent-level splits of the same 102 videos (n=58, 31, 13). They are not extracted as separate rows because the paper's headline is the overall 17% and splitting would double-count the same videos; the exact values are recorded here. (2) Source-category splits of the 17% (Table 4: foundation/medical 5/38 = 13%, news/media 1/8 = 13%, industry/for profit 7/35 = 20%, independent medical professionals 1/3 = 33%, independent non-medical users 3/18 = 17%) are likewise subgroups of the same corpus, not distinct cells. (3) Per-therapy shares (corticosteroids 5%, N-acetylcysteine 6%, enzymes 4%, cannabis oil 2%, stem cells 2%, each 1% for the rest) are components of the 17%; summing them would be a forbidden cross-category sum (R8) and they double-count videos recommending several therapies. (4) 'Videos addressed a median of 17% (7%-27%) of all content items' and the DISCERN scores are medians of a scale with no share above a threshold, so no row (completeness, not falsity). (5) '66% of all videos suggested at least one guideline-recommended therapy' is a share of CORRECT content, not misinformation. (6) '10% of all videos had a primary focus of advertising specific products' is a commercial-intent share, not a falsity share. (7) 'Videos recommending non-indicated therapies had nearly 10-fold higher viewership' is a relative comparison with no share of views attributable to misinformation, so NO exposure or concentration row can be built despite the paper reporting view counts (median 1380 views, IQR 341-8509). (8) '8 of 18 independent non-medical videos (44%) were posted by individuals who claimed to be patients with IPF' is a source-composition figure, not a misinformation share.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis, single search date (4 May 2017), US version of YouTube with cleared history/cookies and a US IP. Frame: first 200 results (10 pages) for the exact phrase 'idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis'; 173 unique videos, 102 eligible after excluding duplicates, non-IPF, non-English, no-audio and non-patient-directed videos (only the most recent upload kept for 13 multi-segment playlist videos). Every video downloaded and saved. Two clinician raters (a respirology fellow and an ILD-subspecialised respirologist) independently scored content against 30 guideline-derived items, HONCode (8 principles) and DISCERN (16 items). Reliability: content median agreement 96%, kappa 0.85 (0.81-0.96); HONCode median agreement 95%, kappa 0.77; DISCERN median agreement 75%, kappa 0.61. Multivariate linear regressions adjusted for source, duration, continent, days online, rank. Authors' limitations: single search term, single date, playlist segments scored lower, no viewer demographics, industry category mixes pharma with supplement sellers, DISCERN validated for written not video material.
rob.item6_quote: An IPF educational video was defined as any video posted on YouTube that described the definition, symptoms, risk factors, diagnostic tests, management, and/or outcomes of IPF. ... Content was evaluated using a predefined scoring system based on 30 key IPF features that are described in previous and recent clinical practice guidelines.
rob.item10_quote: Therapies that are not recommended in clinical practice guidelines were suggested in 17% of videos, including corticosteroids as a chronic treatment in 5% of videos and N-acetylcysteine in 6%.
